title: Latency-quality tradeoff matrix for batching & KV-cache configs
creator: Ava Patel
description: Goal: Quantify the latency vs quality tradeoffs across candidate batching and KV-cache configurations and produce a decision matrix + automated regression alerts. This ticket grows out of intermittent customer reports of slower p95 latency after enabling larger batch windows and a suspected small drop in summarization quality for long-context prompts. We need a controlled eval harness, a reproducible matrix of configs, and thresholds to tie to alerting and rollout policies.
background: Recent autoscaling and batching improvements allowed larger in-flight batch sizes (up to 32) and more aggressive KV-cache prefetching. Preliminary load tests (ENG-9310) showed 1.6x throughput at batch=16, but a few hand-checks indicated quality regressions on long-form summarization and instruction-following tasks when cache prefetch is enabled with shorter TTLs. Product wants a conservative rollout path (canary + automated rollback) if quality drop exceeds tolerances.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible evaluation harness that runs the same prompt suites across all config cells (batch size x cache mode x cache TTL)
A latency matrix with p50/p95/p99 and token/sec for each cell under representative QPS profiles
Quality metrics per cell: automated pairwise A/B win-rate vs baseline, ROUGE-L for summarization, and embedding-similarity for semantic fidelity
Defined thresholds for automated regression alerts (e.g., <=-3% win-rate or >=+10ms p95) and documented rollback policy
A PR with config knobs and monitoring dashboard links + runbook for operators
test_plan: Assemble prompt suites: Summarize-Long (1k-3k tokens), Instruction-Follow (complex multi-step), Chat-Context (multi-turn 30 messages)
Define baseline config: batch_size=1, cache=on TTL=3600s, model=rw-instruct-v3 (canonical eval model)
Define matrix: batch_size in [1,4,8,16], cache_mode in [off, read-only, aggressive], TTL in [60,300,3600]
Run each cell under two load profiles: low (5 qps) and peak (120 qps) using perfbench clusters
Collect latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput (tokens/sec), memory/GPU utilization, and save generated outputs
Run automated pairwise A/B comparisons (10k samples per cell where feasible) against baseline using redwood-evals harness
Log all outputs to S3 and index per-run metrics in the perf dashboard; snapshot differences for human review
results_summary: Early runs (batch=8, cache aggressive, TTL=60) improved throughput by ~1.9x at peak but showed a -4.3% pairwise win-rate on Summarize-Long and ROUGE-L drop of 2.1 points vs baseline. Latency p95 improved for short prompts but regressed for long-context summarization due to cache eviction churn. Batch=4 with cache read-only and TTL=300 maintained throughput gains (~1.3x) with <=1.0% win-rate delta and no significant ROUGE regression. Detailed matrices and raw artifacts are in the links below.
observations: Aggressive cache prefetching with short TTL introduces KV churn for long contexts, increasing p95 for long outputs despite better median latency
Large batch sizes can mask token-level latency regressions for long generations, leading to worse user-perceived latency for interactive flows
Pairwise A/B win-rate correlates strongly with ROUGE-L for summarization tasks but less so for instruction-following where hallucination rates matter
CPU-to-GPU transfer and kernel warmup patterns caused initial tokens latency spikes at batch boundaries for batch>=16
decision: Do not enable batch>=8 + aggressive cache by default for hosted customers; treat as opt-in experimental profile
Adopt batch=4 + cache read-only + TTL=300 as conservative default for Dedicated where throughput is prioritized but quality must be preserved
Add automated regression alerts: trigger if pairwise win-rate <= -3% OR ROUGE-L delta <= -1.5 OR p95 regression >= +12ms relative to pinned model baseline
Instrument canary rollout job that runs redwood-evals on incoming config changes and gates traffic ramp based on metric thresholds
next_steps: Ship follow-up PR that adds the eval matrix runner to infra (github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4721) and a pipeline step in CI
Wire alert rules into Ops: create Kibana/Alerting rules and a Slack channel with runbook link
Schedule human review of top 3 failing prompts per cell for product & research on 2026-03-18
Prepare customer communication template for Dedicated customers describing opt-in performance profiles
